facts.statement: The genus was first described by Qiang Ji and colleagues in 2003.
facts.quote: Shenzhousaurus was first described by Qiang Ji, Mark Norell, Peter J. Makovicky, Keqin Gao, Shu-An Ji and Chongxi Yuan in 2003

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in fluvial beds of the Aptian-aged Yixian Formation at the Sihetun site in western Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: The holotype (NGMC 97–4–002, National Geological Museum of China) was collected from near the bottom (fluvial beds) of the Yixian Formation (Aptian) at the Sihetun fossil site, Beipiao, western Liaoning Province.

facts.statement: The holotype is a partial skeleton preserved in a 'death pose' with the head positioned above the torso.
facts.quote: This specimen consists of a partial skeleton preserved on a sandstone slab in a "death pose," its head above the torso.

facts.statement: The holotype is missing the distal hindlimbs, most of the tail, most of the forelimbs, and the pectoral girdle.
facts.quote: The distal parts of the hindlimbs, distal portion of the tail, and the forelimbs (except for part of the right hand) and the pectoral girdle are missing.

facts.statement: The skull of the holotype is crushed and exposes the left side obliquely.
facts.quote: The head is crushed, exposing the left side obliquely.

facts.statement: The holotype skull measures 185 mm in length.
Pebbles found in the thoracic cavity of the holotype have been interpreted as gastroliths.
facts.quote: A number of pebbles found in the thoracic cavity have been interpreted as gastroliths.

facts.statement: The genus is monotypic and is phylogenetically positioned between Pelecanimimus polyodon and Harpymimus oklandikovi.
facts.quote: The genus is currently monotypic and appears to be more derived than Pelecanimimus polyodon, yet less derived than Harpymimus oklandikovi.

facts.statement: Shenzhousaurus lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Shenzhousaurus is a basal ornithomimosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of China.
rejected.quote: Shenzhousaurus (meaning "Shenzhou lizard") is a genus of basal ornithomimosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of China.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'basal ornithomimosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous'

rejected.statement: Shenzhousaurus is distinguished by a straight ischial shaft, an acuminate posterior end of the ilium, a metacarpal I that is half the length of metacarpal II, and dentition restricted to the symphyseal portion of the dentary.
rejected.quote: It may be distinguished from the latter by its "straight ischial shaft and acuminateposterior end of the ilium" and from all other ornithomimosaurs excepting Harpymimus by the relative length of metacarpal I (only half that of metacarpal II) and in that its reduced dentition is restricted to the symphyseal portion of the dentary.
